kevin: Quick announce — we flipped the Hosted default request routing policy from `latency-first` to `hybrid-cost-latency`. Canary ran for 24h on mixed GPU/CPU fleets and the metrics look promising. Rolling to 10% now, will ramp if stable.

kevin: TL;DR: median generation latency down ~12% for async text workloads, mean token cost down ~22% for small/medium seqs, peak p99 latency up ~6% on a handful of models but still within our soft SLO. See details and traffic plan below. :rocket:

natalie: can you drop the canary dashboards + the exact numbers for chat flows vs single-shot? want to check convo SLO impact.

kevin: dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/canary/hybrid-routing-2245619876 (auth required)
chat flows (aggregated): median -9%, p95 -5%, p99 +4% (within 300ms soft SLO); single-shot/text-gen: median -14%, p95 -18%, p99 +7% on very large sequence lengths. Overall token-cost improvement driven by better batching and lower fallback to larger-variant kernels.

kevin: Canary config (snippet):
```yaml
routing_policy: hybrid-cost-latency
weight: 0.10  # canary fraction
priority_buckets:
  - latency_threshold_ms: 250
    prefer: low_latency_models
  - latency_threshold_ms: 500
    prefer: cost_efficient_models
fallbacks:
  - on_high_p99: fallback_to: compatible_low_latency_variant
  - on_region_capacity: fallback_to: regional_backup
```

infra-bot: deploy: rollout started by kevin at 2245619930 to hosted-prod cluster (10% traffic). Logs: https://deploys.redwood/internal/2245619930

sara: For Dedicated customers — does this change their routing or billing behavior?

kevin: No change for Dedicated. Dedicated customers keep `latency-first` by default to honor SLA-backed capacity. Hosted-only default changed; customers can still pin a route config to override. Example override to force latency-first:
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "routing_policy": "latency-first"
}
```

mike: heads-up watchlist: small-batch (<8 tokens) requests saw the p99 bump. Recommend enabling the auto-fallback to low-latency variant at 95th percentile crossing and consider a microbatch window adjustment.

kevin: agreed. I pushed an immediate tweak to fallback thresholds and added a microbatch window increase for sub-8 token requests. Rollback criteria: if p99 increases >15% over baseline for more than 30m or error-rate >0.5% for any model variant, we rollback to latency-first.

alaric: :thumbsup: nice win.

kevin: Please keep an eye on traces in #eng-runtime and attach any anomalous payloads. I'll post a 48h summary with per-model deltas and follow-up recommendations. Thanks everyone! :tada:
